title: Chrome Lines
description: A pool of liquid chrome on acid yellow-green paper, drawn only in engraved lines. Each line is a stripe of one screen bent by the surface it lies on, so one diagonal cut bows over the forms and crowds into moiré where the surface turns fast, and the stroke carries the tone without ever going solid: it swells until the lines nearly merge where the chrome reflects the dark studio, and thins to a violet hairline where it catches a softbox, with peach and lilac plates slipping out of register through the mid-tones. The sheet is not flat: it sags into dimples and saddles, and in three places it opens clean through to the paper, each hole rimmed by its own standing lip. Press and hold to dent the mirror; hold longer and the dent goes through. Pull it and it behaves like mercury: a drop necks off on a thread, holds, and snaps back into the pool when you let go; at rest it breathes.
intent: herb's generative art reference 1 (liquid chrome blob as a directional line halftone on acid yellow-green). One process pushed to the edge: a height field of spring-driven metaballs is lit by a hard studio environment and then printed as a single line screen whose phase is displaced by the surface, with per-plate misregistration giving the iridescent fringe.
sources: herb generative art reference 1: liquid chrome line halftone on acid ground
